transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because for the past few months, the property manager and some people in my building have been trying to pressure me out of my apartment. It’s things like misdelivered mail, noises timed through the walls, and little comments from neighbors. They give explanations and paperwork, but it doesn’t change the pattern I’m seeing.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds when no one was around, that others couldn't hear?
No, I haven’t heard voices when nobody was there. The sounds I’ve noticed seem to be coming from the building, as far as I can tell.
How has your mood been over these past few months?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I’ve been focused on dealing with the situation at the building, but I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a particular change in my mood.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled, placed into your mind, or broadcast so others could hear them?
No, I haven’t felt that my thoughts were being put into my mind or sent out for other people to hear.
Before these past few months, have you generally found it difficult to trust the intentions of people in your life?
I wouldn’t say I’ve generally had that problem. I try to judge people by what they do, and usually I’ve been able to trust the people in my life well enough.
Have you been diagnosed with any medical or neurological conditions?
No, I haven’t been diagnosed with any medical or neurological condition that I’m aware of.
Outside of dealing with this issue in your building, how has your ability to work and manage your daily life been?
Outside of the apartment situation, I’m managing okay. I handle my finances, cook for myself, and keep my appointments. I can still talk about my consulting work or painting in an organized way.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a circumscribed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion involving the property manager and neighbors attempting to force them out of their home, persisting over several months. Daily functioning, cognition, and affect outside this specific belief system remain well-preserved, and there is an absence of hallucinations, thought disorder, mood episodes, or medical/substance etiologies, fulfilling criteria for persistent delusional disorder.

confirmed_symptoms: Persecutory beliefs that the property manager and neighbors are systematically working to pressure the patient out of their apartment
Delusional interpretation of coincidental events (misdelivered mail, wall noises, casual comments)

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Delusional beliefs have been present continuously for the past few months (at least 3 months)
additional_requirements: Absence of prominent or persistent auditory hallucinations
Absence of thought alienation (thought broadcasting, insertion, or withdrawal)
Preserved functioning and organization outside the circumscribed delusional system
No evidence of underlying medical or neurological conditions
